member: Tomas - Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Analyst
message:
Elena, Marcus, Priya, the springs sag a fist height under weight and still shake clear of stops. In plain words the coil carries steady weight plus crowd shake without bottoming, then the numbers that decide are the static sag calculation (E55) of 72.3 mm from the TMD weight calculation (E35) of 4.90 kN on the stiffness in the TMD stiffness and viscous coefficient (E24) of 67.8 kN per m, plus the dense-crowd stroke scaling (E53) of 20.1 mm giving the total compression calculation (E56) of 92.4 mm, about hand width and fitting below deck with the plus-minus 50 mm dynamic stops in the bolted frame sketch (E37).

Elena, Marcus, Priya, the hidden Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, secondary mass tuned to the bridge mode) keeps dense-crowd shaking comfortable. In plain words violent becomes gentle bus braking, then the numbers that decide are the TMD-controlled acceleration scaling (E52) of 0.545 m per s squared, 0.0556 times gravity, below the 1.00 m per s squared minimum bound in the Experimental and Numerical Study on Dynamics of Two Footbridges (E38).

Ready, because static plus dynamic travel, stop margin and comfort now close jointly.
